children.text: The rail names every panel under its icon. Chats is a list first: each thread shows a picture of what it works on, so the right one is found by sight, and opening one gives the thread with its scope pinned at the top.

64 px wide, a 10 px label under each 18 px icon. Design adds Layers and Assets above the shared panels; Vibe and Prototype share the rest. The dot that says an agent is working belongs to the icon's own box: absolute in its top-right corner, over the glyph with a ring in the panel's colour, so nothing moves when it comes and goes. Pink, as everything an agent does.
No account and no login: the circle is git's user.name, and its email sits in the popup it opens. Set apart from Settings by a rule, so the two are not pressed by mistake.
From git config in this repository
Signs your comments on the canvas
The scope's picture, the title, the last line of the thread, and who works on what. Working, waiting for you or stopped closes the meta line; unread is a dot by the time.
Which alarm types should it offer?
The agent exited: out of credit.
The pin shows the warehouse name.
What the thread was started on decides the picture: the element, drawn by the preview; the page's first screen; a stack for several elements; the agent's mark when there is no scope.

Attached elements are chips with their own picture, in their selection colour (purple for a component), removable one by one. Add to chat on the canvas adds a chip here; so does dragging a layer in. While the agent works, what is typed is queued.

Right-click any element for a link that opens the editor on its page with it selected and in view, or for its ID. The ID is the node's own, kept in the page file, so it lasts as long as the element: the editor's MCP tools take it as it is. In another space it reads marketing:/pricing#id.
The thread can leave the panel and float over the canvas, as a window the size of a phone, so the page it changes stays in view. The panel button puts it back.
Order id first, then device, quantity, customer, status and date.
